notes: Select several songs in the library and you can now drop them straight into a playlist. The multi-select bar had Create album, Add to album, Export and Delete but no playlist action at all, so the only way in was to open each song, tap ⋮ and add it one at a time. There is an add-to-playlist button in the bar now, and it uses the same picker as a single song — it shows which playlists already hold your selection, counts the ones that do (2/5), and still asks where in the playlist they should land. Adding several songs is one insertion, not one per song, and a song already in that playlist is never duplicated
Tapping a playlist your whole selection is already in takes them all back out again, the same toggle the single-song picker has always had, and selection mode closes when you are done

Exports saved an empty or half-finished file, and the app called it a success. Three separate faults added up to that, all of them in the native save path only — a browser export was fine. Capacitor’s writeFile has no append option, so every 256KB chunk of a backup was written over the last one and only a fragment survived; chunks are now appended with appendFile, which is the only real append the plugin has

The zip-writing path batched its chunks as already-encoded base64. A 64KB chunk is not a multiple of three bytes, so each chunk ended in “=” padding and the phone’s decoder stops at the first padding it sees — a batched write kept just its first chunk. The batch now holds raw bytes and is encoded once when it is flushed, so only the very end of the file can be padded

A written file is verified before anything is announced. The export now stats the file it just created and refuses to call it done if it is missing or holds no bytes, instead of handing the 0-byte path to the share sheet with an “Exported” message — and a chunk write that fails no longer resolves as a finished export, so it falls back instead of lying. Downloads to your phone are checked the same way
